messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — High 429 rates detected for /v1/generate on pool hotpath-1 (us-west-2). Queue growth > 1k reqs. Triggering paging to #incidents. Link: https://metrics.redwood/internal/graphs/ghJk
oncall-ryan: I'm on it, coming up. mounting dashboards now. what's the observed customer surface?
prod-support: multiple customer reports — chat latency/timeouts. Ticket RED-4321: "intermittent 429s, attempts to retry fail". Affects PRO tier and some STD routes.
nashok: looking at cluster: hotpath-1 pool nodes=8 (max configured), pending queue 1200, avg latency for token accept loop increased from 30ms -> 450ms. Autoscaler logs show repeated 'scale_up suppressed: max_nodes_reached' and 'scale_up_queued: cooldown'.
maria: quick config check: route rate limits show tokenbucket: scope=global, burst=100, refill=100/s for 'standard' tier. That looks wrong — we intended per-pool limits.
sarah: confirmed — a recent ratepolicy merge (PR #4876) unintentionally changed scope to global when applying a safety cap. probably allowed low burst across all pools.
oncall-ryan: ok immediate mitigation checklist: 1) disable global tokenbucket cap 2) bump hotpath-1 max_nodes to 20 3) shorten autoscaler cooldown to 30s 4) enable fallback to coldpool v2 for non-PRO traffic. I'll coordinate.
nashok: doing step 1 now — patching ratepolicy live:
```
PATCH /config/ratepolicies/global
{ "tokenBucket": { "enabled": false }
}
```
deploy-bot: Deployment queued: config/ratepolicies/global -> patch (rolling) by oncall-ryan. CI ok.
maria: I can confirm tokenbucket disabled at global scope; per-pool limits still present. Traffic in metrics shows slight drop in 429s but queue still heavy.
eng-infra-rotation: taking over for scaling ops. I'll set max_pool_nodes to 20 and trigger a force-scale.
kevin: watch out for coldstart blowup — if we scale too fast the aggregate GPU allocation may exceed quota. what's the org quota in us-west-2?
nashok: current project GPU quota is 24 gpus. scaling to 20 nodes (1 GPU each) should be ok but we need to ensure other pools (batch, embed) don't push us over. I'll trim batch temporarily.
oncall-ryan: bulk actions:
- increase hotpath-1.max_nodes=20 (eng-infra)
- autoscaler.cooldown_ms=30000 (ashok)
- set route fallback: non-PRO -> coldpool v2 (maria)
- monitor 429, queue length, latency (sarah)
eng-infra-rotation: applied max_nodes=20 and issued scale_force for hotpath-1. nodes provisioning started.
nashok: shortened cooldown to 30s in autoscaler config and restarted scaler instance (rolling restart). logs: "cooldown set to 30000ms".
maria: fallback route change applied: standard tier now has fallback to coldpool-v2 for non-critical routes. This should shed ~25% of hotpath load.
sarah: metrics update (T+2m): queue dropped from 1200 -> 400, 429s dropped from 28% -> 12%. Latency improving but still elevated.
prod-support: customer RED-4321 updated — confirmed fewer errors, but still seeing occasional 429s. They asked for ETA to normal.
oncall-ryan: ETA depends on node readiness. If all 12 nodes come up we should be back to normal in ~5-10m. continuing to monitor and will update.
nashok: noticed autoscaler still emitting 'scale_up_suppressed: tier_token_limit' messages for some routes — looks like per-tier token limit for 'standard' set to 150/s across pool members, which is too low under burst. I'll tune tokenburst per-tier to 500 for hotpath traffic.
maria: please apply conservative step: per-tier tokenRefill=500 and burst=1000 for hotpath routes. doing now.
nashok: patched tier policy:
```
PATCH /config/tiers/standard
{ "tokenBucket": { "refillPerSecond": 500, "burst": 1000 }
}
```
deploy-bot: Deployment success for /config/tiers/standard.
sarah: T+8m: queue ~90, 429 rate 1.8%, p95 latency nearly baseline. PRO tier unaffected. Looks stable.
prod-support: updated RED-4321: customer acknowledges recovery, will keep case open for follow-up.
oncall-ryan: post-handoff: Handoff to eng-infra for follow-up and postmortem. Key actions captured in incident doc: https://docs.redwood/incidents/2134567890
eng-infra-rotation: taking postmortem action: 1) revert erroneous global tokenbucket change in PR workflow, 2) add unit/integration test to ensure ratepolicy scope is preserved, 3) add an automatic guard that prevents global caps from applying to pools with hotpath label.
kevin: also recommend autoscaler alert: alert if scale_up suppressed due to max_nodes for >1m and queued_requests >200.
maria: adding onboarding note for Product: communicate to customers if PRO vs STD differences in throttling.
nashok: root cause hypothesis: config change in ratepolicy merge applied global cap; during sudden traffic surge, global cap throttled token issuance, causing bursts to queue while autoscaler hit pre-set max_nodes and cooldown, preventing scale to handle load -> 429s. Mitigation removed global cap, raised per-tier token rates, and expanded pool capacity.
oncall-ryan: final status: incident mitigated, impact reduced to minor; continuing monitoring for 2 hours. Will file P0->P1 classification for follow-through. :thumbsup:
